name: Wayne Gretzky
milestone_by_age_26: At age 17, signed a seven-year personal services contract with the Indianapolis Racers of the WHA worth $1.75 million; at 18, won the Lou Kaplan Trophy as WHA rookie of the year with 110 points and played in the WHA All-Star Game alongside Gordie Howe.
early_history_summary: Gretzky began skating at age two on his grandparents' farm and was taught hockey by his father Walter on a backyard rink. By age six he played with ten-year-olds, and by his mid-teens he was dominating junior hockey in Ontario, scoring 132 points in 60 games in Junior B. At 16 he joined the Sault Ste. Marie Greyhounds, and at 17 he signed with the WHA's Indianapolis Racers, later traded to the Edmonton Oilers where he won rookie of the year.
family_context_summary: Born to Walter and Phyllis Gretzky in Brantford, Ontario; Walter was a telephone company technician who built a backyard rink and devoted extensive time to coaching Wayne and his brothers in hockey.
parent_family_domain_summary: Walter Gretzky was not a professional hockey player but was a dedicated amateur coach who taught Wayne and his siblings hockey fundamentals on a backyard rink, providing sustained individualized training from a very young age.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father-coach,backyard rink,early specialization,junior hockey pipeline,WHA opportunity
evidence_summary: Gretzky's father Walter built a backyard rink and provided sustained hockey coaching from age two, giving Wayne thousands of hours of practice before his teens. By age six he played with ten-year-olds, and by 17 he was signed to a $1.75M professional contract. The WHA's lack of an age-20 minimum (unlike the NHL) created a structural opportunity for his early professional entry. His scoring dominance at every level before 18 demonstrates exceptional early specialization and concentration.
starting_point: Born to a middle-class family in Brantford, Ontario; father Walter was a telephone company technician who built a backyard rink and devoted extensive time to coaching Wayne and his brothers in hockey.
current_position: Retired NHL legend; net worth estimated ~$250M; resides in the United States; part-owner and vice-chairman of Oilers Entertainment Group (left 2021), now NHL analyst on Turner Sports.

trajectory.event: Signed a seven-year, $1.75M personal services contract with the Indianapolis Racers of the WHA, later traded to the Edmonton Oilers.
Won the Lou Kaplan Trophy as WHA rookie of the year with 110 points; Oilers joined the NHL via the WHA merger.
Led the Edmonton Oilers to their first Stanley Cup championship, beginning a dynasty of four titles in five years.
Scored 215 points in a single NHL season, an all-time record; won his sixth consecutive Hart Trophy as NHL MVP.
Traded to the Los Angeles Kings in a blockbuster deal, credited with popularizing hockey in the American Sun Belt.
Inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame after retiring as the NHL's all-time leader in goals, assists, and points.

name: Esa-Pekka Salonen
milestone_by_age_26: At age 25, replaced an indisposed Michael Tilson Thomas on short notice to conduct Mahler's Symphony No. 3 with the Philharmonia Orchestra in London, a performance that launched his international conducting career.
early_history_summary: Salonen graduated from one of Finland's top high schools in 1977 and studied horn, composition, and conducting at the Sibelius Academy under Jorma Panula. He first conducted the Finnish Radio Symphony Orchestra in 1979 at age 21. His 1983 last-minute substitution with the Philharmonia in London, conducting Mahler's Third without having studied the score, became the breakthrough that established him internationally.
family_context_summary: Born in Helsinki, Finland; family background not documented in reviewed sources beyond his education at top Finnish schools.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Sibelius Academy,Jorma Panula,top high school,Finnish conducting tradition,Philharmonia opportunity
evidence_summary: Salonen attended SYK, one of Finland's top high schools, and then the Sibelius Academy where he studied conducting under the renowned pedagogue Jorma Panula alongside classmates who also became major conductors. The Sibelius Academy provided elite training and a peer network in Finnish classical music. His 1983 Philharmonia debut was a chance opportunity enabled by his training and readiness, but the institutional pipeline from SYK to Sibelius to professional conducting was the key advantage.
starting_point: Born in Helsinki, Finland; attended one of the country's top high schools (SYK) before entering the Sibelius Academy for horn, composition, and conducting studies.
current_position: Principal conductor designate of Orchestre de Paris and creative director designate of the Los Angeles Philharmonic; music director of San Francisco Symphony 2020-2025; conductor laureate of multiple major orchestras.

trajectory.event: Made his conducting debut with the Finnish Radio Symphony Orchestra.
Replaced Michael Tilson Thomas on short notice to conduct Mahler's Symphony No. 3 with the Philharmonia Orchestra in London, launching his international career.
Made his US conducting debut with the Los Angeles Philharmonic.
Became music director of the Los Angeles Philharmonic, a position he held for 17 years.
Became principal conductor and artistic advisor of the Philharmonia Orchestra in London.
Won the Grawemeyer Award for his violin concerto written for Leila Josefowicz.
Became music director of the San Francisco Symphony.

name: Magnus Wislander
milestone_by_age_26: At age 21, debuted for the Swedish national handball team (January 16, 1985) and won the Swedish championship with Redbergslids IK in the 1984-85 season; named Swedish handball player of the year in 1986 at age 22.
early_history_summary: Wislander started playing handball at Tuve IF in Gothenburg at age nine, before joining Redbergslids IK in 1979 at age 15. He became a senior player for Redbergslids IK starting in 1983 at age 19, won the Swedish championship four times with the club, and debuted for the Swedish national team in January 1985 at age 21. By 1986 he was named Swedish handball player of the year.
family_context_summary: Born in Gothenburg, Sweden; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early club specialization,Redbergslids IK,Swedish handball pipeline,physical size
evidence_summary: Wislander joined a top Swedish handball club (Redbergslids IK) at age 15 and became a senior player at 19, providing years of high-level reps before his national team debut at 21. Sweden was a dominant handball nation, and the Gothenburg club ecosystem gave him early access to elite-level training and competition. His physical stature (1.96m) was an asset in handball. Family background is not documented in reviewed sources.
starting_point: Born in Gothenburg, Sweden; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Retired from professional handball in 2005; worked as a handball coach until 2022 and as a handball commentator; voted Handball Player of the Century by the IHF.

name: Roberto Clemente
milestone_by_age_26: At age 18, signed with Cangrejeros de Santurce in the Puerto Rican Professional Baseball League; at 19, signed with the Brooklyn Dodgers for a $10,000 bonus; at 20, made his MLB debut with the Pittsburgh Pirates on April 17, 1955, recording his first career hit.
early_history_summary: Clemente grew up in Carolina, Puerto Rico, and was a track and field star before focusing on baseball. He began his professional career at 18 with Santurce in the Puerto Rican winter league, was signed by the Brooklyn Dodgers in 1954 with a $10,000 bonus, assigned to the Montreal Royals minor league team, and then drafted by the Pittsburgh Pirates in the 1954 Rule 5 draft, making his MLB debut at 20.
family_context_summary: Born in San Anton, Carolina, Puerto Rico; the youngest of seven children in a working-class family; father worked as a foreman on a sugar plantation and mother ran a grocery store.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources as having direct baseball domain expertise in the family, though Clemente grew up in a baseball-rich Puerto Rican culture.
primary_early_advantage_tags: working-class Puerto Rico,early pro signing,baseball-rich culture,athletic talent,bonus rule
evidence_summary: Clemente grew up in a working-class family in Puerto Rico where baseball was culturally dominant. He was a multi-sport athlete who turned to baseball professionally at 18, quickly attracting the attention of MLB scouts. The bonus rule of the era created a structural opportunity for the Pirates to acquire him from the Dodgers. His path from Puerto Rican winter ball to MLB by 20 was driven by raw athletic talent and early domain immersion rather than family resources or elite training pipelines.
starting_point: Born to a working-class family in Carolina, Puerto Rico; father was a sugar plantation foreman and mother ran a grocery store; youngest of seven children.
current_position: Died December 31, 1972 at age 38 in a plane crash off the coast of Puerto Rico while delivering earthquake relief supplies to Nicaragua; final role: Pittsburgh Pirates right fielder and 12-time All-Star.

name: Demetrios Christodoulou
milestone_by_age_26: At age 19-20, completed a PhD in physics at Princeton University under John Archibald Wheeler, with a doctoral thesis on gravitational collapse and black hole physics; became a full professor at the University of Athens at age 21.
early_history_summary: Christodoulou was a prodigy in Athens who taught himself advanced mathematics and was profiled in local newspapers as a 'Student-Einstein.' Through a family connection, he met physicist John Archibald Wheeler in Paris in 1968, who invited him to Princeton. He entered Princeton at 16, earned his MA in 1970, and completed his PhD by 1971 at age 19-20, followed by a full professorship at the University of Athens at 21.
family_context_summary: Born in Athens, Greece; a family friend, mechanical engineer Spyros Michalopoulos, connected him to physicist Achille Papapetrou, which led to the meeting with John Archibald Wheeler that opened the path to Princeton.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources as having academic domain expertise, though the family had a connection to a mechanical engineer (Spyros Michalopoulos) who facilitated the introduction to the physics community.
evidence_summary: Christodoulou was a self-taught mathematical prodigy in Athens whose abilities were noticed through a family connection to a mechanical engineer, leading to an introduction to physicist Achille Papapetrou and then to John Archibald Wheeler. Wheeler invited him to Princeton at 16, where he completed his PhD by 19-20 under Wheeler's supervision. The mentorship from Wheeler and the Princeton institutional ecosystem were critical accelerants, but the foundation was his exceptional self-driven intellectual depth.
starting_point: Born in Athens, Greece; a self-taught mathematical prodigy who was discovered through a family connection to a mechanical engineer who introduced him to the physics community.
current_position: Emeritus professor of mathematics and physics at ETH Zurich since 2017; honorary professor at the University of Crete; holds dual Greek and U.S. citizenship.

trajectory.event: Entered Princeton University as a graduate student in physics on the recommendation of John Archibald Wheeler.
Completed his PhD in physics at Princeton under Wheeler with a thesis on gravitational collapse and black hole physics.

Named a MacArthur Fellow; published the proof of the stability of Minkowski space coauthored with Klainerman.

Awarded the Shaw Prize in Mathematical Sciences.

name: Gilbert & George
milestone_by_age_26: In 1969 at age 26 (Gilbert's age), performed 'The Singing Sculpture' at the National Jazz and Blues Festival, their first major public artwork that launched their career as 'living sculptures.'
early_history_summary: Gilbert Prousch (born 1943 in South Tyrol, Italy) studied art at schools in Sëlva, Hallein, and the Kunstakademie Munich before moving to London. George Passmore (born 1942 in Plymouth) studied at Dartington College of Arts and Oxford School of Art. They met at Saint Martin's School of Art in September 1967 and began collaborating immediately, creating 'The Singing Sculpture' in 1969, their breakthrough performance piece.
family_context_summary: Gilbert was born in San Martin de Tor in South Tyrol, Italy, a Ladin-speaking region; George was born to a single mother in a low-income household in Plymouth, England, and dropped out of school by 15.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources as having art-world family connections; George's low-income background is noted.
primary_early_advantage_tags: art school collaboration,Saint Martin's,living sculpture concept,1960s London art scene,low-income background
evidence_summary: Gilbert and George met at Saint Martin's School of Art in 1967 and immediately formed a collaborative duo that became their core creative advantage. George came from a low-income single-parent household, while Gilbert came from a Ladin-speaking village in South Tyrol. Their complementary partnership and the concept of 'living sculpture' were their primary advantages, emerging from the vibrant 1960s London art scene. The Singing Sculpture, first performed in 1969, was recognized as the piece that launched their career.
starting_point: Gilbert born in a Ladin-speaking village in South Tyrol, Italy; George born to a single mother in a low-income household in Plymouth, England; both studied art before meeting at Saint Martin's School of Art in London in 1967.
current_position: Active as artist duo; opened the Gilbert & George Centre in East London in April 2023 to showcase their work; celebrated 50th anniversary of collaboration in 2017.

trajectory.event: Gilbert and George met at Saint Martin's School of Art in London and began their artistic collaboration.

Elected to the Royal Academy of Arts; celebrated 50th anniversary of their collaboration.

name: Bruno Sammartino
milestone_by_age_26: At age 24 in 1959, set a world record in the bench press with a lift of 565 pounds (256 kg) without elbow or wrist wraps, and made his professional wrestling debut; by 25, he was already headlining Madison Square Garden.
early_history_summary: Sammartino grew up in poverty in Pizzoferrato, Italy, surviving the German occupation during WWII. He emigrated to Pittsburgh in 1950 at age 15, began weightlifting to overcome bullying, and developed extraordinary strength. In 1959, he set a world bench press record of 565 lbs and made his pro wrestling debut, quickly becoming a major attraction at Madison Square Garden by 1960.
family_context_summary: Born in Pizzoferrato, Abruzzo, Italy to a family of seven; grew up in extreme poverty during WWII under German occupation; emigrated to Pittsburgh in 1950 where his father worked in a quarry.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources as having wrestling or athletic domain expertise in the family.
primary_early_advantage_tags: WWII survival,immigrant,poverty,weightlifting self-creation,physical strength,Pittsburgh wrestling scene
evidence_summary: Sammartino's path was defined by extreme adversity: childhood poverty and wartime survival in Italy, immigration to Pittsburgh at 15, and bullying that drove him to weightlifting. His extraordinary physical strength (world record bench press of 565 lbs at 24) was self-developed through intense training. A local landscaper introduced him to weightlifting, and University of Pittsburgh coach Rex Peery trained him in wrestling. The Pittsburgh wrestling ecosystem and his physical prowess were the key advantages that enabled his rapid professional rise.
starting_point: Born to a large impoverished family in Pizzoferrato, Italy; survived the German occupation during WWII; emigrated to Pittsburgh in 1950 at age 15 where he began weightlifting to overcome bullying.
current_position: Died April 18, 2018 at age 82 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania; final role: WWE Hall of Famer (inducted 2013), considered one of the greatest professional wrestlers of all time with the longest world title reign in wrestling history (2,803 days).

trajectory.event: Set a world record in the bench press with 565 lbs and made his professional wrestling debut in Pittsburgh.

Inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame after years of estrangement from the organization.
Died on April 18, 2018, in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.

name: Sérgio Santos
milestone_by_age_26: At age 25 in 2001, debuted for the Brazilian national volleyball team and won his first FIVB World League gold medal, beginning a career that would make him the greatest libero in volleyball history.
early_history_summary: Sérgio Dutra dos Santos grew up in the periphery of São Paulo and worked as a supermarket packer, office boy, and street vendor during adolescence. He started his club career at SE Palmeiras in 1992 at age 17, played for CRET São Caetano from 1997, and first played in the Superliga in 1996. When the libero position was created in 1998, he was between clubs and selling bleach door-to-door before adapting to the new position and being called to the national team in 2001.
family_context_summary: Grew up in the periphery of São Paulo in a low-income family; worked multiple menial jobs during adolescence including as a supermarket packer, office boy, and street vendor.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources as having volleyball or athletic domain expertise in the family.
primary_early_advantage_tags: low-income background,Brazilian volleyball pipeline,libero position creation,Palmeiras,early club career
evidence_summary: Santos grew up in poverty in São Paulo's periphery, working menial jobs while pursuing volleyball. He started at Palmeiras at 17 and was playing in the Superliga by 1996. The creation of the libero position in 1998 was a structural opportunity that fit his defensive skills. Brazil's dominant volleyball culture and national team pipeline provided the ecosystem for his rise. His national team debut at 25 in 2001, winning World League gold, was the qualifying milestone.
starting_point: Born in Diamante do Norte, Paraná, Brazil; grew up in the periphery of São Paulo in a low-income family; worked as a supermarket packer, office boy, and street vendor during adolescence.
current_position: Retired from professional volleyball in 2020 at age 44; considered the greatest libero in volleyball history; two-time Olympic gold medalist (2004, 2016) and 2016 Olympic MVP.

name: Ralph M. Steinman
milestone_by_age_26: No material, independently verifiable career milestone by age 26 found. Steinman completed his M.D. from Harvard in 1968 at age 25, but his defining achievement—the discovery of dendritic cells—occurred in 1973 at age 30, and the Nobel Prize came in 2011.

name: Boris Vallejo
milestone_by_age_26: At age 13, obtained his first professional illustration job in 1954; at 16, attended the Escuela Nacional Superior Autónoma de Bellas Artes in Lima on a five-year scholarship and was awarded a prize medal for his artistic ability.
early_history_summary: Vallejo was born in Lima, Peru, and began painting at age 13. He obtained his first illustration job that same year (1954). At 16, he earned a five-year scholarship to Peru's national art school (Escuela Nacional Superior Autónoma de Bellas Artes), where he won a prize medal. He emigrated to the United States in 1964 at 23 and built a career illustrating fantasy and science fiction book covers.

name: Manny Ramirez
milestone_by_age_26: At age 19, was drafted 13th overall by the Cleveland Indians in the 1991 MLB draft with a $250,000 signing bonus and named Appalachian League MVP; at 21, made his MLB debut on September 2, 1993, and was named Minor League Player of the Year by Baseball America; by 23, was an MLB All-Star and Silver Slugger winner.
